ae17f931af2f8606: Torque peaks at 5,000 rpm at 300 lb-ft. After that torque falls, but the revs are still rising, and the product keeps growing until the fall in torque outweighs the rise in speed. From 5,000 to 6,000 rpm torque drops by 20 lb-ft (6.7%) while rpm rises by 20%, so horsepower climbs from 285.6 to 319.9. From 6,000 to 7,000 rpm torque falls 14.3% and rpm rises 16.7%, which nearly cancels, and the two horsepower figures are equal at 319.9. The peak lies between them. In general the horsepower peak is never below the torque peak, because at the torque peak torque has stopped rising but the revs have not, so the product is still climbing.
